newsitem.title: NEPAL: Maoist rebels kill two policemen in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: Maoist rebels kill two policemen in Nepal.

text.p: Two policemen were killed and three wounded on Thursday in an ambush in western Nepal by Maoist insurgents, government officials said.

A spokesman for the Home (Interior) Ministry said Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) activists attacked six policemen on duty for local elections, scheduled to be held on Saturday, in the Himalayan kingdom's remote Rukum district.
Nepal is holding elections on May 17 and 26 for 4,000 village committees that form the kingdom's local government.

A hardline faction of the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) is opposed to multi-party democracy and is boycotting the elections. The Maoists are seeking to replace the parliamentary system with a government of the "working class".
About 100 people have been killed since the insurgency was launched 15 months ago in nine remote districts of Nepal. The latest killings take the death toll in election-related violence to seven.
A multi-party system was established in Nepal in 1990 after pro-democracy demonstrations that whittled down the king's absolute powers.
